title: Ashfield Systems integration tidbits
content:
Call date: 2024-10-10 with Ashfield Systems (prod ops + infra lead) - short brain-dump and next steps.

Context:
- Customer: Ashfield Systems — chain of ~120 small-format retail outlets across Northeast.
- Use case: in-store agent for returns and inventory lookup; must work on intermittent cellular/Wi-Fi at stores.
- Preferred: Private deployment in their VPC (govc rated) but budget constrained — exploring dedicated-reserved vs private with hybrid edge cache.

Key technical constraints stated on call:
1) Edge connectivity is flaky: average RTT to cloud region ~180-400ms from some stores, frequent short disconnects (30–90s).
2) Store hardware: Intel NUC-class boxes, 8GB RAM, one low-end NVIDIA T4 (some sites have no GPU).
3) Data residency: transaction logs must stay in their VPC; embeddings allowed to be aggregated but must be encrypted at rest/transport.
4) SLA expectation: 95th percentile response < 700ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens). Bulk batch syncs allowed offline.

Product-fit notes / ideas:
- Hybrid approach seems best: Redwood Private control plane + local microservice for edge caching and offline request queue. Local microservice runs small quantized model (gpt-small-ish) where GPU exists; otherwise uses CPU quantized runtime.
- Use Redwood caching primitives: prefix/KV cache on the local microservice to avoid repeated context fetches during brief reconnects.
- Suggest model tiering: primary hosted model (runnable in Private control plane) + fallback very-small local model for degraded connectivity. Fallback outputs intentionally shorter and marked with a special metadata flag so client can surface to ops.

Gotchas / risks from call (capture raw):
- "We can't open arbitrary egress to hosted endpoints": their security team will block unless we provide explicit IP list and a transit VPN.
- On-device inference ops unknown: some stores never had drivers updated; GPU driver mismatches likely.
- Bandwidth costs: frequent embedding calls for search/recall could balloon their egress billing if we require centralization.
- Telemetry: They want token-level cost attribution by store but also strict PII redaction upstream. Need to confirm which fields are PII before shipping logs.

Quick config sketch (for later write-up):
- VPC Private control plane in us-east-1, peered to Ashfield VPC via TGW + VPN.
- Local agent container with these components:
  * local-llm (quantized fp16/int8) with model store (auto-update disabled by default)
  * request-queue (durable, on-disk) with exponential backoff to central
  * prefix-kv-cache (LRU, 256MB cap) for recent dialog state
  * telemetry-forwarder (redact hook before egress)
- Routing policy: prefer local-llm for prompt if latency budget < 700ms and connectivity healthy; else route to private control plane and use cached fragments to reduce token count.

Performance/quality tradeoffs to discuss with product/research:
- Quantized local models vs hallucination/quality: need eval harness for Ashfield prompt set to measure degradation.
- When to prefer central model for quality-sensitive tasks (refund justification text) vs local for fast answers (inventory counts).

Immediate next steps (who/when):
- Maya: draft technical sketch for solutions review (due 2024-10-18). ACTION: include config diagram + fallback rules.
- Liam: schedule follow-up call with Ashfield infra (VPN/IP ranges) and ask for a sample store network report (due 2024-10-20).
- Priya: assemble short eval prompt set (10–15 queries) from product to measure local vs central model quality (due 2024-10-25).
- CS: open JIRA CS-7421, link to Confluence page (existing link above).

Questions still open (to resolve before PoC):
- What exact driver/kernel versions are in their field fleet? If many are old, we will need a CPU-only fallback or a managed driver upgrade plan.
- Can they accept a small local model binary with a 1-year license (security wants review)? Need legal to confirm.
- Token-level telemetry: is per-store attribution enough, or do they need per-terminal? Ask during infra call.

Notes from random side-discussions:
- They mentioned a legacy SOAP endpoint for inventory lookup. We should propose a thin adaptor that normalizes to our vector-store lookups; this will reduce prompts and tokens.
- They would pay a small fee for a one-off field visit (pilot) to validate on-device GPU behavior. Worth asking solutions eng budget to support.

Draft messaging for follow-up email to Ashfield (short):
- Recap top approach: hybrid Private control plane + lightweight local agent with caching + clear fallback rules.
- Ask for: (1) sample network report for 3 stores; (2) list of store terminal models + OS/drivers; (3) approval to share a small on-device binary for security review.
- Propose next call week of 2024-10-21 (tech + security).

Misc small todo (internal):
- Add a short entry to the private-deploy checklist about "offline queue durability" and "local cache encryption at rest".
- Add sample prompts to product-hosted-api eval bucket for Ashfield.

Bottom line: good candidate for Private + hybrid edge. Primary blockers: networking (VPN/egress policy) and field hardware variability. Prioritize short eval to quantify quality drop on quantized local model vs central.

End of scratchpad.
